extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent training staff, and external stakeholders (applicants, practitioners) participating in examiner training
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for training patent examiners (and external stakeholders) to examine and produce high-quality patents, covering legal analysis, claim interpretation, searching, office action writing, and technical/site exposure. The document describes training program goals, course modules (STEPP), workshop content, and evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving Clarity and Reasoning (ICR) – make clarity integral
rubrics_metrics.description: To include as an integral part of all substantive training tips and techniques for enhancing the clarity of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should provide not only identification of examination topics, but also a focus on clarity of the Office action through relevant examples. The Office is working to identify ways to improve training delivery, including using workshop-style training for certain topics and delivering training by small groups of select trainers to improve consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal topics coverage (112(a), 112(b), 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops and training modules covering statutory/legal areas including 112(a), 112(b), and 35 U.S.C. 101 (multiple workshop levels referenced as 101 II, 101 III).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training includes workshops and presentations on written description/claim definiteness (112(a), 112(b)) and subject-matter eligibility (101), presented at refresher and master levels with examples to improve examiner understanding and application in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Analysis and Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Training on legal analysis and writing to improve the quality and clarity of written Office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offered as a workshop topic (FY17). Emphasizes structuring legal reasoning, clarity of explanations, and consistent articulation of grounds for rejection or allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on claim interpretation as a foundational step when reading an application for the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STEPP Day 1 focuses on the role of an examiner and the steps an examiner would take when reading an application for the first time; claim interpretation and 35 USC 101 and 112 are emphasized on Day 1 to inform searching and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search planning and mapping prior art (35 U.S.C. 102 and 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and conduct a search, and map prior art to claims using 35 USC 102 (novelty) and 103 (obviousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STEPP Day 2 uses the information gathered during Day 1 to plan a search, conduct a search, and map prior art to claims. Training should teach practical search techniques and how to relate prior art to claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action drafting, restriction practice, and post-examination options
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in writing of an Office action including restriction practices and knowledge of post-examination options such as the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) and the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STEPP Day 3 focuses on office action writing and restriction practices; includes discussion of appeal/reexamination paths to ensure examiners communicate grounds and options clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Training on properly documenting and explaining Reasons for Allowance when claims are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a refresher/master level topic; aims to improve quality and clarity of the record regarding why claims are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Training to improve examiner skill and practice in applicant interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes presentations and practice sessions; listed among FY16 modules. Training metrics show high participant agreement that interview practice training improved understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) and accurate classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Training on Cooperative Patent Classification to ensure correct classification of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPC included as a presentation topic (FY17) to aid consistent and proper classification, which supports searching and examination quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case law awareness (Case Law Year in Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping examiners current on relevant case law that affects examination practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a course topic to ensure examiners apply up-to-date legal precedent in analysis (FY17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refresher and Master training for experienced examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Refresher Training: designed for examiners with at least one year of experience. Master Training: dives deeper into specific legal areas for examiners with at least one year of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refresher and Master classes delivered periodically (FY16 counts given). Use to deepen substantive knowledge and reinforce consistent application of law and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PETTP – technical state-of-the-art training
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary technical seminars by technologists, scientists, and engineers to provide examiners technical training and expertise regarding the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes in-person and virtual presentations (various locations). Aims to improve examiner familiarity with real-world technologies to support more informed prior art searches and analysis. FY16 metrics: 173 seminars, 37,423 hours, reached 77% of examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEE – Site Experience Education (site visits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Site visits to commercial, industrial, and academic institutions to provide technical training and improve examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO funds travel for site visits within continental US. Purpose: interact with real-world technologies, conduct on-site training, and showcase technologies to examiners. FY16 spending and trip counts provided as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management and supervisory training to support quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Training for managers and supervisors on leadership, coaching, mentoring, giving feedback, and managing telework to enhance examiner performance and patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Management Training Academy, continuing training topics (e.g., Encouraging and Motivating Employees, Dealing with Difficult Situations, Giving Constructive and Meaningful Feedback). Monthly training provided to over 800 patent managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examining for Non-Examiners (PEFNE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training for non-examining internal stakeholders focused on the life of an application and the role of a patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to give non-examiners perspective on examination practice; FY16/FY17 participation numbers included.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEPP purpose: increase transparency and aid compact prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose external stakeholders to USPTO training on examination practice and procedure to increase transparency, provide examiner perspective, and aid compact prosecution by disclosing how examiners are taught to use the MPEP to interpret an applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current course: 3-Day Training on Examination Practice and Procedure, expected to train ~300 attendees in FY17. STEPP is tiered (webinars, workshops, multi-day courses) in proposed expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MPEP to interpret an applicant’s disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Training to show external stakeholders how examiners are taught to use the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) to interpret an applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to promote compact prosecution by aligning applicant and examiner understanding of MPEP-based interpretation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training evaluation metrics (participant feedback items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant survey items used to evaluate training effectiveness, including: I understood the learning objectives; This course was easy to follow; There was sufficient time; The information is relevant and applicable; Instructor knowledge enhanced learning; Ample opportunity to discuss; Materials aided learning; My knowledge and skills increased; I plan to apply knowledge and skills; I would recommend this course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STEPP and other courses report average scores (e.g., 4.9/5) for many items. Use these items to measure training effectiveness and guide improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training delivery format and scale considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use workshop structures, numbers of trainers, training duration, and number of sessions to achieve coverage and effectiveness (examples: 5-week 101 Workshop III with 44 trainers and 5,079 examiners; 71 sessions for 112(b) Workshop covering 300 art units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust trainer-to-examiner ratios, session counts, and make-up time to balance reach and depth; small-group delivery is recommended to improve consistency.
